claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain relative to commercially used pure tungsten under plasma-facing service conditions.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under plasma-facing service conditions.
The proposed enhancement is governed by a refined, homogeneous microstructure and improved grain-boundary cohesion.
Ta, Ti, V, and Zr are low-activation refractory alloying elements in WTaTiVZr.
Ta, Ti, V, and Zr are uniformly distributed in the proposed WTaTiVZr microstructure.
The alloying elements alter the local chemistry at WTaTiVZr grain boundaries.
Altered grain-boundary chemistry reduces brittle intergranular fracture.
The alloyed microstructure promotes more uniform dislocation motion.
Spark-plasma sintering can produce bulk equimolar WTaTiVZr with a homogeneous, fine-grained microstructure.
Commercially processed pure tungsten typically has a coarse, brittle microstructure.
Testing WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten under identical high-temperature loading conditions isolates the effect of alloying-induced microstructural changes.
Temperatures of approximately 800–1200 °C are representative of high-temperature plasma-facing-component service.
Alloying tungsten with Ta, Ti, V, and Zr yields a solid solution.
Alloying tungsten with Ta, Ti, V, and Zr refines the microstructure and enhances grain-boundary cohesion.
The refined and cohesive microstructure permits more active dislocation nucleation and mobility under high-temperature stress.
WTaTiVZr should exhibit a statistically significant increase in tensile plastic strain relative to pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr should exhibit statistically significantly higher fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
Fractured WTaTiVZr should show more ductile, transgranular features and fewer brittle intergranular features than pure tungsten.
Formation of deleterious secondary phases may invalidate the proposed plasticity and toughness mechanism.
The proposed mechanism may not hold at temperatures much lower than 800 °C.

contradictions.description: The initial-state description compares spark-plasma-sintered, fine-grained WTaTiVZr with commercially processed, typically coarse tungsten, whereas the falsification design says both materials will be made using identical manufacturing and processing routes. These are materially different control designs.

The intervention claims to isolate alloying-induced microstructural changes, but the stated initial states deliberately differ in both composition and grain structure. This comparison cannot separately identify grain refinement, grain-boundary chemistry, and bulk compositional effects.
